title: Problem Overview
content: **Erdős Problem #828** asks whether for every integer a, there are infinitely many natural numbers n such that φ(n) | n + a. This is a sweeping generalization of two classical problems: the completely solved a = 0 case (where φ(n) | n iff n is a 3-smooth number times a power of 2) and the famous open Lehmer's conjecture (a = -1, asking whether φ(n) | n - 1 forces n to be prime). The conjecture is attributed to Graham and appears in Guy's 'Unsolved Problems in Number Theory'.
mathContext: The totient function φ(n) = |{k ≤ n : gcd(k,n) = 1}| is multiplicative with φ(p^k) = p^{k-1}(p-1). The condition φ(n) | n + a links the multiplicative structure of n to a linear shift.

title: Totient Divisors Set
content: **totientDivisors(a)** = {n ∈ ℕ : φ(n) | n + a} is the central object of study. The definition works over ℤ to handle negative values of a naturally: (totient n : ℤ) ∣ (n : ℤ) + a. The conjecture asks whether this set is infinite for every a ∈ ℤ. For a = 0, the set includes 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, ... (the 3-smooth numbers). For a = -1, the set is exactly the primes (assuming Lehmer's conjecture).
mathContext: Using ℤ arithmetic avoids issues with natural number subtraction. For example, when a = -1, we need φ(n) | n - 1, which is cleanly expressed as (φ(n) : ℤ) | ((n : ℤ) + (-1)).

title: Special Case a = 0: Complete Characterization
content: **totient_dvd_self_iff** axiomatizes the classical result: φ(n) | n if and only if n ≤ 1 or n = 2^a · 3^b with a > 0. The key insight is the formula φ(n)/n = ∏_{p|n}(1 - 1/p): for φ(n) | n, this product must be 1/k for some integer k, which happens only when the prime factors are 2 and 3 (giving 1/2 and 2/3 respectively). **totientDivisors_zero_infinite** follows immediately since 2^a · 3^b gives infinitely many solutions.
mathContext: The 3-smooth numbers (numbers whose prime factors are at most 3) form a well-studied class. The characterization shows that φ(n) | n is equivalent to n being 3-smooth with at least one factor of 2.

title: Lehmer's Conjecture (a = -1)
content: **lehmerConjecture** is defined (not axiomatized) as the statement that for n > 1, φ(n) | n - 1 iff n is prime. The easy direction is proved constructively: **prime_totient_dvd_pred** shows φ(p) | p - 1 using Mathlib's `totient_prime` (which gives φ(p) = p - 1). The hard direction (no composite Lehmer number exists) has been open since 1932. It is known that any composite Lehmer number must be odd, square-free, and have at least 15 prime factors. **totientDivisors_neg_one_infinite** axiomatizes that infinitely many n satisfy φ(n) | n - 1 (the primes suffice).
mathContext: A composite Lehmer number would be a counterexample: a composite n > 1 with φ(n) | n - 1. No such n has been found despite extensive computation up to 10^30.

title: The Main Conjecture (OPEN)
content: **erdos828Conjecture** states the full open problem: for every a ∈ ℤ, the set totientDivisors(a) is infinite. This is a universal statement over all integers, packaging infinitely many individual infiniteness questions. The two known cases (a = 0 characterized, a = -1 with primes) support the conjecture, but extending to arbitrary a requires understanding the interplay between the multiplicative structure of φ and additive shifts.
mathContext: The conjecture is attributed to Graham. Even showing totientDivisors(a) is nonempty for all a would be nontrivial, though the infiniteness claim is much stronger.

title: Structural Properties of the Totient
content: Three key properties of Euler's totient function. **totient_even**: φ(n) is even for all n > 2 (since -1 is a unit in (ℤ/nℤ)*, making elements come in ±pairs). **totient_prime'**: a Mathlib wrapper confirming φ(p) = p - 1 for primes. **totient_prime_pow_formula**: φ(p^k) = p^{k-1}(p-1) for prime powers. Together these control the divisibility φ(n) | n + a when n has specific prime power structure.
mathContext: The evenness of φ(n) for n > 2 means that φ(n) | n + a requires n + a to be even when n > 2. This gives immediate parity constraints on solutions.

title: Summary Theorem
content: **erdos_828_summary** combines the two main known results: totientDivisors(0) is infinite (the 3-smooth numbers) and totientDivisors(-1) is infinite (the primes). The proof is constructive, using `exact ⟨totientDivisors_zero_infinite, totientDivisors_neg_one_infinite⟩` to build the conjunction from the two axioms. This captures the complete state of rigorous knowledge: the conjecture is verified for a = 0 and a = -1, but open for all other values of a.
mathContext: The conjunction type (totientDivisors 0).Infinite ∧ (totientDivisors (-1)).Infinite is the strongest statement the formalization can make without resolving the full conjecture.
